row.evidence: If a meromorphic representative has domain D=U, it is holomorphic on U by Definition clause (a)(2), and it itself supplies the extension in clause (c). A proper dense open domain may have removable omissions: the zero function on U minus one point extends holomorphically to U and has no pole. Thus D!=U does not imply any pole; poles are defined by failure of local holomorphic extension.

template_review.reason: The actual definition explicitly permits holomorphic extensions across removable omissions. Its reverse full-domain clause follows from holomorphy on D, while proper-domain representatives can extend with no poles; the corrected note states precisely those two cases.
